stories.headline: Hit-and-run driver kills pedestrian near Federal Boulevard and West 66th Avenue in Berkley
stories.summary:
A 38-year-old Denver man was killed and a 46-year-old Denver man was seriously injured Monday night after a white Ford F-150 struck them while they were crossing Federal Boulevard near West 66th Avenue in the Berkley neighborhood, between Denver and Westminster. The driver fled the scene, and investigators later found the vehicle abandoned less than half a mile away near Decatur Street and West 67th Place.

Colorado State Patrol troopers responded to the crash just after 9:15 p.m. and were actively searching for the driver as of Tuesday afternoon, with no suspects publicly identified or arrested. The case remains under investigation.

The Berkley intersection where the crash occurred is a high-traffic corridor connecting Denver and Westminster. Authorities are urging anyone with information to come forward as the search for the suspect continues.

stories.headline: 500-teen crowd vandalizes, loots Aurora shopping center; 70 officers respond
stories.summary:
A crowd of approximately 500 teenagers descended on the Hoffman Heights shopping center near East Sixth Avenue and North Peoria Street in Aurora on Sunday afternoon following an unpermitted sporting event, quickly devolving into vandalism and theft at nearby businesses including a restaurant and a grocery store. Aurora Police declared an unlawful assembly and required more than 70 officers to disperse the group.

Aurora Police Chief Todd Chamberlain said investigators are reviewing video and other evidence to identify those suspected of criminal activity. No arrests were publicly announced as of Tuesday.

The incident is the latest in a series of so-called 'teen takeovers' that have disrupted public spaces across the Denver metro area in recent years. Anyone with information can contact Metro Denver Crime Stoppers at 730-913-7867.

stories.headline: Denver man arrested on suspicion of first-degree murder in August road-rage shooting that killed passenger
stories.summary:
Lino Sandoval, 23, was arrested last week on suspicion of first-degree murder and attempted first-degree murder in connection with an Aug. 21 shooting on the edge of Denver's West Colfax neighborhood near Federal Boulevard and West 17th Avenue, the Denver Police Department announced Monday. A passenger in the targeted vehicle was shot and later died at the hospital; the driver called 911 while fleeing the pursuing car.

Surveillance cameras captured a white SUV following the victims' car in Lakewood near West Sixth Avenue and Sheridan Boulevard, roughly three miles from where the shooting occurred. Police used the footage to identify Sandoval, who was arrested on Friday and is being held without bail at the Downtown Detention Center.

Sandoval is scheduled for a review hearing Thursday morning in Denver court. The case remains a developing investigation.

stories.headline: Update: Denver resident identified as man killed when truck plowed into Tour de Fat crowd in Fort Collins
stories.summary:
The Larimer County coroner's office has identified the man killed when a pickup truck drove onto a crowded Fort Collins sidewalk during the annual Tour de Fat festival Saturday as Joshua Robert Douglass, 33, of Denver. Douglass died of blunt force injuries, the coroner announced Tuesday.

Douglass and at least four other pedestrians were struck when the pickup reversed out of a parking spot, struck another vehicle, and drove onto the sidewalk. The driver and the four surviving victims were all taken to a hospital.

Detectives are continuing to investigate the crash, including whether impairment was a factor. Authorities said Saturday that it does not appear any of the pedestrians were targeted.

stories.headline: Latino support for Trump collapses in Colorado's competitive 8th Congressional District, new poll shows
stories.summary:
A new poll commissioned by the Colorado Latino Policy Agenda found that 61 percent of Latino voters in Colorado's 8th Congressional District now disapprove of President Donald Trump, a sharp reversal from summer 2025 when 54 percent of the same demographic approved of his job performance. The district, centered on the northern Denver suburbs, is roughly 40 percent Hispanic and is considered one of the most competitive congressional seats in the country.

The poll, conducted by BSP Research among 288 Latino voters in the 8th District, also found that 70 percent disapprove of Trump's overall job performance, up from 42 percent a year ago. Republican Rep. Gabe Evans, who won the seat by less than a percentage point in 2024, drew a 34 percent approval rating among Latino voters compared to 42 percent disapproval.

Despite the erosion in support for Trump and Evans, the race is not a lock for Democratic challenger and state Rep. Manny Rutinel of Commerce City, with just 51 percent of Latino voters backing him. Latino voters in the district cited cost of living, wages and housing affordability as their top concerns, with 44 percent saying their financial situation had worsened over the past year.

stories.headline: Waymo launches public self-driving car service in Denver
stories.summary:
Waymo officially began offering rides to the general public in Denver on Tuesday, marking the autonomous vehicle company's entry into the Colorado market after several months of training runs on city streets. Residents can now hail a driverless Waymo vehicle through the company's app within the designated service area.

The launch makes Denver one of a small number of U.S. cities where Waymo operates a fully public commercial service. The company has been expanding beyond its original markets in Phoenix, San Francisco and Los Angeles.

The rollout is expected to draw attention to ongoing regulatory and infrastructure questions around autonomous vehicles in Colorado, including insurance requirements and the city's role in overseeing the technology on public roads.

stories.headline: Denver advances $4.5 million design contract for Red Rocks backstage overhaul
stories.summary:
A Denver City Council committee unanimously approved a $4.5 million contract Tuesday with engineering firm SEH Inc. to design a major backstage renovation at Red Rocks Amphitheatre, converting the underground performer area into a five-story facility. The project, funded through the voter-approved $950 million Vibrant Denver bond package passed in 2025, will add new dressing rooms, showers, an elevator, covered parking, a kitchen and dining area, and bring the facility into ADA compliance for the first time since it was constructed in the 1940s.

Venue director Tad Bowman told the committee that some performers currently have difficulty navigating the aging ramps to the stage. Councilwoman Amanda Sawyer pressed officials to confirm that the iconic exposed rock visible inside the dressing rooms would be preserved, which Bowman confirmed.

The new structure will be designed partly underground to maintain audience sightlines to the city skyline from the seating bowl. Construction is expected to begin in November 2027 and will be carried out only during the venue's five-month off-season to avoid disrupting performances, with roughly $30 million in bond funds allocated for the construction phase.

stories.headline: Rockies end franchise-record 10-game home losing streak with 4-2 victory over Orioles
stories.summary:
TJ Rumfield broke a seventh-inning tie with a two-run home run Tuesday night as the Colorado Rockies defeated the Baltimore Orioles 4-2 at Coors Field, snapping their franchise-record 10-game home losing streak. The Rockies had not won at home since an 8-1 victory over Kansas City on Aug. 2.

Adael Amador, called up from Triple-A Albuquerque earlier in the day, opened the scoring with a solo home run in the second inning. Jaden Hill earned the win and Jordan Romano closed out the game with a 1-2-3 ninth inning for his 14th save.

The Orioles, who dropped to 69-70, fell 1.5 games behind Cleveland for the final American League wild card spot. The two teams wrap up their three-game series Wednesday afternoon.

stories.headline: Avalanche 2026-27 season preview: Makar deal locked in, Nichushkin traded, MacKinnon seeks redemption
stories.summary:
With the 2026-27 NHL season approaching, the Colorado Avalanche head into the year having locked in defenseman Cale Makar on the richest contract in league history and retooled a roster that reached the Western Conference Final before being swept by Vegas. The Avs' offseason saw general manager Chris MacFarland depart for Nashville, with Joe Sakic resuming full GM duties.

Colorado traded Valeri Nichushkin to Columbus to clear cap space and sent Ross Colton, Jack Drury and Isak Posch to Nashville. In return, the team signed Brent Burns to a one-year deal and added depth pieces Jaden Schwartz, Brett Kulak and Noah Juulsen. Nathan MacKinnon, coming off a third consecutive Hart Trophy-caliber season, is described as particularly motivated following a critical missed opportunity against Team USA.

Gabriel Landeskog, who returned to regular-season play last year for the first time since the 2022 Stanley Cup championship, will anchor the second line alongside Nazem Kadri and Brock Nelson. The projected top line pairs MacKinnon with Martin Necas, who moves into the spot vacated by traded winger Mikko Rantanen.

stories.headline: Michelin-starred Bruto names Peruvian-trained chef Carolina Zubiate as new culinary director
stories.summary:
Denver's Michelin-starred tasting counter Bruto has hired chef Carolina Zubiate as its new culinary director, restaurateur Kelly Whitaker announced Tuesday. Zubiate, a Peru-born chef who moved to Denver a decade ago, has spent the past three years working double shifts as a cook at James Beard Award-winning Yuan Wonton and running acclaimed Peruvian and Chifa pop-ups at notable venues across the city.

Zubiate succeeds Byron Gomez, who brought Costa Rican influences to Bruto's 18-seat counter at 1801 Blake St., and before him Michael Diaz de Leon, whose tenure focused on Mexican flavors. Under both chefs, Bruto earned three consecutive Michelin stars — a record it will look to extend when the guidebook announces its latest Colorado awards later this month.

Zubiate said she plans to incorporate Peruvian techniques and ingredients — including dishes inspired by anticuchos and pachamanca — into Bruto's existing framework of live-fire cooking and fermentation. Menu development is expected to unfold over months as she integrates with the kitchen team.

stories.headline: Denver's August restaurant scene: Soda Club opens in RiNo, Rock Bottom brand exits metro area
stories.summary:
More than 20 new restaurants debuted in the Denver metro area in August, headlined by the opening of Soda Club, a Michelin Bib Gourmand-recognized New York-based Italian vegan concept, at RiNo's Ramble Hotel. Other notable arrivals include a Louisiana po'boy pop-up called Poor Boys in The Source and a new Enzo's Brick Oven Pizza on East Colfax under new ownership.

On the closure front, the Rock Bottom Brewery brand has officially exited the Denver metro area after its Centennial and Highlands Ranch locations shuttered in August, leaving only a Loveland outpost remaining in Colorado. Chicago Mike's Beef & Dogs in Centennial also closed following the death of its owner, Giles Everist.

A notable preservation came when Edible Beats founder Justin Cucci and the Root Down restaurant group acquired beloved 16-year-old LoHi bakery The Wooden Spoon, saving it from imminent closure. Westword's full August recap lists dozens of openings and closings across the metro area.

stories.headline: Five Denver-area cafes serve as gateways to global coffee cultures
stories.summary:
A growing number of Denver-area coffee shops are using their menus to introduce customers to international cultural traditions, from Filipino-inspired drinks in RiNo to Guatemalan highland teas in Berkeley and LoDo. Coffee Sarap, founded by two daughters of Filipino immigrants, operates out of a RiNo storefront and serves drinks such as an ube latte and Filipino-style horchata alongside food from fellow Filipino American vendors.

Convivio Café, which opened a second location in LoDo earlier this year after its original Berkeley spot, sources beans directly from Guatemalan farmers and serves drinks like the Churrazo, a cinnamon-pinole latte. The Denver Post profiles five such shops in total, also highlighting Indonesian, Indigenous-sourced and Ethiopian coffee traditions represented across the Front Range.

The trend reflects a broader diversification of Denver's coffee scene, which has traditionally emphasized craft roasting and single-origin sourcing. Shop owners say the cultural context behind each cup is as important as the beverage itself.

topStory.headline: Jury Deadlocked in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial; Judge Orders Deliberations to Continue
topStory.summary:
A jury in Plymouth, Massachusetts, informed Judge William Sullivan on Tuesday that it was unable to reach a unanimous verdict in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the 2023 deaths of her children. The announcement drew audible gasps from the courtroom. Sullivan declined to declare a mistrial and instructed the panel of nine women and three men to continue deliberating, with jurors expected back in court Wednesday.

Clancy, 36, does not dispute that she killed her children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and eight-month-old Callan — at the family's Duxbury, Massachusetts, home on January 24, 2023, after sending her husband Patrick out on errands. She was left paralyzed after jumping from a second-floor window following the killings and now appears in court in a wheelchair. Her defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, argues she was in a state of postpartum psychosis and could not distinguish right from wrong, citing forensic psychiatrist Dr. Phillip Resnick, who testified she was psychotic at the time of the deaths. Prosecutors, led by Assistant District Attorney Jennifer Sprague, contend Clancy made a calculated choice, arguing her children were the only factor preventing her from ending her own suffering.

The jury began deliberating last Thursday after a five-week trial that featured testimony from more than 80 witnesses and hundreds of exhibits. Jurors have already requested to review pill bottles and a kitchen knife connected to Clancy's suicide attempt, signaling close attention to the physical evidence. The trial has drawn significant public interest, and a woman was arrested by Massachusetts State Police outside the courthouse Tuesday on an expected charge of intimidating a witness or juror, though police did not confirm a connection to the Clancy case.

If the jury reports a deadlock a second time, Judge Sullivan may issue what is known in Massachusetts as a Tuey-Rodriguez charge — sometimes called a dynamite instruction — urging jurors to consider one another's perspectives while maintaining their honest convictions. A third deadlock report could lead Sullivan to declare a mistrial. Defense attorney Reddington said Tuesday he is prepared to represent Clancy again should a retrial become necessary. A conviction on first-degree murder would carry a mandatory life sentence without the possibility of parole.
